comment: "This course bridges clinical obstetrics with emergency medicine and transport logistics, which is rare. It forces learners to think beyond the hospital walls and consider how geography, infrastructure, and communication shape maternal outcomes."

"The modules on postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) were especially powerful. I learned tools I can use immediately in practice. But beyond the facts, what stood out was the emotional intelligence woven into the training—reminding us that normal vital signs can be misleading, and that vigilance saves lives. It made me feel more prepared, more empowered, and more connected to the mission of safe maternal care."

"What I found most interesting in this course was learning how to manage obstetric emergencies, such as postpartum hemorrhage, preeclampsia, and preterm labor. It was very valuable to see how to make quick, evidence-based decisions and practice skills that help both the mother and the baby."

"The course provided practical, real-world knowledge about maternal and neonatal care that I can apply in emergency situations. Clear explanations of obstetric emergencies, such as postpartum haemorrhage and preterm labour, were very helpful."

"The practical scenarios, illustrated by the cases, were interesting to read and learn from. It allowed the opportunity to reflect on practical scenarios that you have seen and managed at work and allowed me to form a strong association with the content. The layout on the content for the management of each case, in terms of predeparture management and management by retrieval team, was a useful approach and template to use and build on."
"I found this course very helpful information for learning, practical and relevant information about managing obstetrics and gynecological cases while in utmost remote health settings."
"I loved every single aspect of the course, highly valuable! Thank you!"
"I enjoyed this course and it has helped me a lot in my knowledge."
